name: Mo Shuming
current_role: Co-founder (and long-time vice chairman) of Guangdong Mingcrown Group, Dongguan
profile: Dongguan-born entrepreneur who co-founded Guangdong Mingcrown Group (名冠集团) in 1994 with Mo Zhiming. The family conglomerate spans construction, real estate, steel/new materials (Huaguan), Xinhui Port logistics, hotels, schools and a golf club; it is now chaired by Mo Guanliang and ranks among Guangdong's top 500 companies.
interesting_fact: Mingcrown is pivoting into culture-tourism: in March 2026 it won Dongguan's first land auction of the year for RMB 730m to build the Mingcrown Oasis theme-park project, and signed a strategic deal with Tencent Cloud in April 2026.
notes: Very low public profile; the group site names him only as co-founder. A 2012 Xinhui district government page called him vice chairman of Mingcrown. Day-to-day leadership is now Mo Guanliang (chairman) and Mo Guanjing (president). Hurun listed him jointly with Yao Hesong. Best route is the group's corporate email.

name: Chen Wenli
current_role: Former director and co-founder of HNA Group (left the board in March 2020); no current public role found
profile: Chen Wenli was one of the founders of Hainan-based HNA Group in 1993, alongside Chen Feng, Wang Jian and Adam Tan. He held an individual HNA stake (Hurun rich list 2017-2019) and sat on the board. He left the board in March 2020 when a Hainan government working group took control. HNA later went through court-led restructuring in 2021, which wiped out the founders' equity.
interesting_fact: He co-founded HNA, which grew from a provincial airline into a global conglomerate that held stakes in Hilton, Deutsche Bank and Swissport during a record overseas buying spree that ended in 2017.
notes: Very low profile and likely not a viable guest. His wealth was tied to HNA equity that was largely erased in the 2021 bankruptcy restructuring, and other HNA founders were detained in 2021. Source for his 2020 board exit: https://www.mingtiandi.com/?p=43164. No personal channels found.

name: Rohini Nilekani
current_role: Chairperson, Rohini Nilekani Philanthropies; co-founder and director, EkStep Foundation
profile: Mumbai-born former journalist and author whose wealth comes from early Infosys shares held with her husband, Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani. She founded the water NGO Arghyam (2001), co-founded Akshara Foundation and Pratham Books, and now runs Rohini Nilekani Philanthropies, which funds civil society, water, climate, biodiversity and youth causes. She also hosts the Grassroots Nation podcast.
interesting_fact: She set up Arghyam in 2001 with a personal endowment of about Rs 150 crore. She chaired it for 20 years before stepping down in 2021, and she is regularly ranked among India's most generous women philanthropists.
deep_cut_fact: She started her career in 1980 as a reporter at the now-defunct Bombay Magazine, after a degree in French literature from Elphinstone College. In 1998 Penguin published her medical-thriller novel 'Stillborn'. She also writes children's stories (the Sringeri series) for Pratham Books, which she co-founded in 2004.
notes: Accessible and media-friendly: she writes columns, gives talks and hosts her own podcast, so a podcaster pitch could suit her. The best route is the RNP contact email. The X/LinkedIn/Instagram accounts listed are the foundation's, not her personal ones. Her angle is philanthropy and civil society rather than energy or data centres.

name: Huang Tengxin
current_role: Unconfirmed; listed by Hurun against Zuoyou (Shenzhen Zuoyou Furniture / 左右沙发)
profile: Hurun China lists Huang Tengxin (黄腾新) as the wealth holder behind Zuoyou, a furniture business. Shenzhen Zuoyou Furniture (左右家私) is a sofa maker with about 4,000 staff and parks in Shenzhen, Huizhou, Anhui and Sichuan. Public sources name Huang Huakun (黄华坤) as its founder, who started making sofas in Shenzhen in 1986. No source found that links the name Huang Tengxin to the company.
interesting_fact: Zuoyou registered its brand in 1995 and opened China's first 'scenario-style' living-room furniture stores. In 2005 it signed former China women's volleyball head coach Chen Zhonghe as brand ambassador.
notes: Identity unresolved. Hurun's 'Huang Tengxin' may be a transliteration or listing error, or a relative or partner of founder Huang Huakun. Verify against Hurun's Chinese list before any outreach. Baidu and Sogou blocked automated lookups.

name: Dennis Erani
current_role: Private investor; 7.8% beneficial owner of Organogenesis Holdings (Nasdaq: ORGO)
profile: Dennis Erani is a passive ten-percent-group holder of Organogenesis, the Canton, MA regenerative-medicine and wound-care company in which the Ades and Erani families are the largest individual holders. The April 2026 proxy shows him with about 10.0m shares (7.8%), mostly held through family trusts. He holds no board or executive role.
interesting_fact: Organogenesis sells regenerative wound-care and surgical/sports-medicine products. Per the 2026 proxy, Alan Ades (17.3%), Albert Erani (13.9%) and Dennis Erani (7.8%) together hold about 39% of its shares.
notes: Essentially no public profile: no interviews, bio or social accounts found. He appears to be a member of the Erani family (Albert Erani is a separate 13.9% holder), but the exact relationship is unconfirmed. Company contacts reach Organogenesis, not him personally. His filed residential address is deliberately omitted.

name: Lin Xiuhao
current_role: Unconfirmed; listed by Hurun against Heiniu Investment (黑牛投资)
profile: Hurun China (2017-2019) lists Lin Xiuhao (林秀浩) as the holder of 'Heiniu Investment' (黑牛 = Blackcow). The name points to Shantou's Black Cattle/Blackcow Food Co. (黑牛食品), a soy-milk and cereal maker whose listed shell was later renamed Visionox Technology, an OLED display maker. No source retrieved confirms Lin Xiuhao's own role.
interesting_fact: In July 2016 Black Cattle Food sold its whole food and beverage business (soy-milk powder, cereals, sesame paste, nut milks) for CNY 513m to Shenzhen Blackcow Capital Management, and the listed shell pivoted to tech. It is now Visionox, the OLED panel maker.
notes: Identity not verified. Chinese search engines (Baidu, Sogou) blocked automated access, and English sources only show Lin Xiuhai (possibly a relative) as a Blackcow/Visionox director. Confirm via Blackcow Food's pre-2018 annual reports on cninfo.com.cn before any outreach. Very private, with no personal channels.

name: Huangxing
current_role: No executive role found; holds an interest in Wison as the spouse of founder Hua Bangsong
profile: Huang Xing (黄幸) appears on Hurun China (2016-2020) jointly with her husband Hua Bangsong, founder of Shanghai-based Wison Group (惠生集团). Wison started as a chemical-engineering firm in 1997 and now spans energy engineering, offshore/marine fabrication (FLNG) and new energies. HKEX-derived insider data lists her interest in Wison Engineering Services (HK: 2236) as a spousal interest.
interesting_fact: Wison won a 2012 contract for a floating LNG facility off Colombia's coast, an early step into floating-liquefaction vessels. The group now runs Wison New Energies from Shanghai's Zhangjiang Hi-tech Park.
notes: No public profile of her own. The wealth is the Hua family's Wison stake (source on spousal interest: https://test.gurufocus.com/insider/239900/huang-xing). For an energy podcast the natural guest is Wison's leadership (Hua Bangsong or Wison New Energies), reachable via Wison's corporate marketing email. Contacts are company-level only.

name: Murli Kewalram Chanrai
current_role: Member of the Chanrai family behind the Kewalram Chanrai (KC) Group; specific current role not found
profile: Hurun India (2015-2016) lists Murli Kewalram Chanrai as a holder of wealth from the Kewalram Chanrai Group. The Sindhi-origin, Singapore/Malaysia-based family conglomerate has interests in textiles, automobiles, agri-inputs, financial services and palm-residue recycling, and it incubated Olam International in 1989. Public material names other family members (e.g. Narain Girdhar Chanrai, Jagdish Chanrai) as group leaders. No retrievable source describes Murli's own role.
interesting_fact: The Kewalram Chanrai Group set up Olam Nigeria in 1989 to earn hard currency by exporting cashews. Run first from London as 'Chanrai International Limited', it grew into Olam, one of the world's largest suppliers of cocoa, coffee, cotton and rice.
notes: Extremely private family; no personal web presence, interviews or official group website found. His role is unconfirmed, so verify before outreach. A Chanrai-family introduction via Olam/Olam Agri or the KC Group's Singapore office (Kewalram Singapore Ltd) may be the only route.

name: Yang Jiuhong
current_role: Controlling shareholder and co-actual controller, Changzhou Aohong Electronics (SSE: 605058); administrative director of subsidiary Haihong Electronics (per 2020 prospectus)
profile: Yang Jiuhong (b. 1950), from Changzhou, Jiangsu, owned about 58.8% of Aohong Electronics, a printed-circuit-board maker, before its 2020 Shanghai IPO. She controls it jointly with her son-in-law Chen Dinghong, the chairman and general manager. She is not a board member; she is listed as administrative director of the Haihong Electronics subsidiary.
interesting_fact: Aohong is a family-run PCB maker: the 2020 prospectus shows founder Yang Jiuhong and Chairman Chen Dinghong jointly controlling about 93% of shares before the IPO. Under a 2019 supplementary agreement, Chen's decision prevails if the two disagree.
notes: Very private, older controlling shareholder with no media presence. Chairman Chen Dinghong is the public face and the more realistic interview target. Contacts are company-level, from the 2020 prospectus.

name: Lu Runting
current_role: Founder, Chairman, Executive Director and CEO, Goldpac Group Ltd (HKEX: 3315)
profile: Lu Run Ting (盧閏霆), about 71, founded Goldpac, a Zhuhai/Hong Kong maker of bank and payment cards and fintech services. He set up its holding company, Goldpac International, in 1993 and the operating group in 1995. He controls the HK-listed group through Goldpac International (Holding), owning roughly 37%, and in 2025 added the CEO title to his role as chairman.
interesting_fact: He has more than 30 years in the financial-card industry and was a finalist for the CNBC Asia Business Leaders Award in October 2015. Goldpac now also runs UMV, a credit-card benefits and user-community platform for banks.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur, he held management positions at subsidiaries of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) and then founded Goldpac International in 1993. He later earned an MBA from Hong Kong Polytechnic University in 2004, about a decade after founding his company.
notes: Hong Kong-listed founder and still hands-on. The fintech and payments angle fits an entrepreneurship episode. Approach via the published Goldpac IR email. No personal social accounts found.

name: Zhao Hui
current_role: Former chairman and general manager of Jinyuan Environmental (金圆股份, SZSE: 000546); resigned all posts in September 2024
profile: Zhao Hui (赵辉) and his father Zhao Bisheng built Hangzhou-based Jinyuan, a cement maker that diversified into hazardous-waste treatment and lithium resources and is listed as Jinyuan Environmental. They jointly controlled it through Jinyuan Holding. He stepped down in 2024, and in March 2025 his entire 10.79% direct stake was transferred away, leaving his father as sole actual controller.
interesting_fact: In 2021 Jinyuan began a transition into new-energy materials (lithium) and the next year began divesting the cement and building-materials business that had made the family's fortune.
notes: Not recommended for outreach. Jiemian reports he was placed on 'qubao houshen' (released pending criminal investigation). The CSRC opened a disclosure-violation case in Nov 2024, and the Jilin CSRC bureau separately fined him RMB 1.5m. His shares were transferred in a 2025 divorce settlement (source: jiemian.com/article/12120058.html). The Hurun Unicorn-founder tag may belong to a different Zhao Hui.

name: Zhang Zhifeng
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO of the HK-listed Huali group (HKEX: 1756; formerly Huali University Group / China Vocational Education Holdings, now China Science and Education Industry Group)
profile: Guangdong education entrepreneur (about 59) who founded Huali Investment in 1999 and built the Huali private schools in Zengcheng, Guangzhou: Guangzhou Huali College, Huali Technical College and Huali Vocational College. He took the group public in Hong Kong in 2019 and has chaired it since 2017, adding the CEO role in 2021.
interesting_fact: He was named one of the '2005 Outstanding Persons of Education Innovation in China' by a panel including Peking University's School of Education. In 2019 he received a Special Contribution Award for Private Education marking the PRC's 70th anniversary.
deep_cut_fact: In September 2005 he received an 'Outstanding Contribution Award' from the Anna Chan Chennault Educational, Scientific and Cultural Award office, named after the Chinese-American journalist and widow of Flying Tigers commander Claire Chennault. He also served on the Zengcheng CPPCC.
notes: HK-listed private-education founder whose company has been renamed twice, so search under HKEX code 1756. The only published channel is the group IR email. Education is off-topic for an energy/data-centre show unless the angle is vocational or tech training.

name: Hu Qingzhou
current_role: Founder, Chairman and controlling shareholder, Shenzhen Yitoa Intelligent Control (英唐智控, SZSE: 300131)
profile: Hu Qingzhou (b. 1968) founded Yitoa Electronics in Shenzhen in July 2001 and built it into a ChiNext-listed electronic-components distributor. Since 2020 he has steered it toward semiconductor manufacturing (IDM), starting with the purchase of Pioneer Micro Technology from Japan's Pioneer Corp. He still chairs the company, holding about 8.5% as of April 2026.
interesting_fact: In 2020 Yitoa bought Japanese chipmaker Pioneer Micro Technology for about 3bn yen, a rare Japan-approved Chinese chip acquisition. In late 2025 it announced further 'dual-chip' deals for Guilin Guanglong Integrated Technology and Shanghai Aojian Microelectronics.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur he worked at the Huaibei (Anhui) tax bureau and at ICBC's Shenzhen branch. He studied at University of Science and Technology Beijing (BS 1991) and earned a management master's from Tianjin University in 2000, a year before founding Yitoa.
notes: Active chip-industry founder; the semiconductor localisation and IDM-pivot story could suit an entrepreneurship episode. Best route is the board-secretary/IR email from the 2026 interim report. His stake has shrunk through pledge-related transfers, so avoid that topic.

name: Sun Li
current_role: Chairman, General Manager and legal representative, Xiamen Amoytop Biotech (特宝生物, SSE STAR: 688278); co-actual controller
profile: Sun Li (孙黎) leads Xiamen Amoytop Biotech, founded in 1996 and focused on long-acting recombinant protein drugs, especially peginterferon for chronic hepatitis B. He controls the company jointly with Yang Ying under an acting-in-concert agreement. He holds about 8% directly, and his spouse Cai Zhihua, listed jointly with him by Hurun, holds 2.8%. In October 2026 the controllers pledged not to sell for five years.
interesting_fact: In October 2025 China approved Amoytop's Pegbing (peginterferon alfa-2b) in combination with antivirals to clear hepatitis B surface antigen. China Daily called it the world's first domestically developed drug approved for a functional cure of hepatitis B.
notes: Biotech founder-operator with a strong recent milestone (hepatitis B functional-cure approval). The topic is outside energy/data centres but suits an entrepreneurship episode. The only published route is the company's general email; no personal channels found.

name: Feng Shaode
current_role: Listed by Hurun China 2021 as a Tsingshan (青山控股) shareholder; specific role not confirmed
profile: Hurun China 2021 lists Feng Shaode (冯绍德) as deriving wealth from Tsingshan, the Wenzhou-founded stainless-steel and nickel giant started by Xiang Guangda in 1988. Tsingshan has a broad base of early Wenzhou partner-shareholders, and Feng is presumably one of them, but no retrievable source confirms his stake or role.
interesting_fact: Tsingshan moved into Indonesian nickel in 2009 and helped build the Morowali Industrial Park in Sulawesi, with at least 20 smelters, making it central to the global stainless-steel and EV-battery nickel supply chain.
notes: Identity and role unverified: Chinese registry sites were not usable, and the web-search budget ran out before more checks. He is likely a passive minority shareholder with no public profile. For an energy/battery-metals episode, Tsingshan's leadership (Xiang Guangda) is the relevant figure.

name: Yan Jinyuan
current_role: Chairman, Guangdong Biolight Meditech (宝莱特, SZSE: 300246)
profile: Yan Jinyuan (燕金元) chairs Biolight, a Zhuhai-based medical-device maker. It was founded in 1993 as a joint venture, became a national industrialisation base for multi-parameter patient monitors in 2003, and listed on the Shenzhen ChiNext board in 2011. It now covers patient monitoring and life support, kidney/dialysis care and home medical devices. Hurun lists him jointly with Wang Shi.
interesting_fact: Biolight began in 1993 as Zhuhai Biolight Electronics, a joint venture. In 2003 China's NDRC designated it the 'national multi-parameter monitor industrialisation base', and it later grew a large haemodialysis business.
deep_cut_fact: Besides running Biolight, he is an associate professor at Xi'an Jiaotong University and a senior engineer, so he is an academic engineer turned industrialist. He has also served as a deputy to the 10th Zhuhai Municipal People's Congress.
notes: The company publishes separate media-cooperation (brand@) and IR emails, so the media email is the best route. Medtech rather than energy. The web-search budget ran out, so his age and current shareholding were not re-verified.
